method: Compiled from dated public sources only (exchange/bank statements as quoted by outlets, court/regulatory filings, and news from CoinDesk, The Block, Bloomberg, Reuters/Kitco, WSJ-via-ForkLog, Cointelegraph, Finance Magnates and others). Compiled blind to price data: no files under data/, reports/rescue/*.json or configs/usd_rail_impairments.json were opened, so labels are independent of any detector output. Dates are UTC calendar dates; where a source gave only a local time or a conflicting date this is stated in notes. Many pages could not be fetched (403 / timeout); entries relying only on search-result summaries say so in notes. Coverage is not exhaustive: absence of an entry is NOT proof of no event.

episodes.description: Wells Fargo (correspondent for Bitfinex's four Taiwan banks) stopped processing outbound USD wires; Bitfinex reported USD withdrawal delays and sued Wells Fargo (suit later dropped).
episodes.notes: First report date is the earliest source I could verify (SiliconANGLE, updated 2017-04-09; CoinDesk 2017-04-11 says suit filed 'late last week'); a Bitfinex announcement a few days earlier is likely but not verified. Start date: NYAG settlement says 'late March 2017'; one compiled timeline says 2017-03-31 (secondary). Outbound wires only per the complaint; no documented end date.

episodes.description: Bitfinex said its Taiwan banks would refuse all incoming wires in every fiat currency from 2017-04-18 and told customers to stop sending wires until further notice (OKCoin paused USD deposits the same day).
episodes.notes: Bitfinex's own notice is quoted by the outlets, not retrieved directly. No restoration date documented; Bitfinex moved to Crypto Capital for retail fiat flows afterwards (see BFX-2018-01).

episodes.description: Bitfinex posted a notice (r/bitfinex) about delayed fiat deposits and withdrawals executed 2018-01-10 to 2018-02-05, blaming a backlog; Crypto Capital was by then the main fiat processor.
episodes.notes: Notice text and 2018-02-20 date come from a compiled timeline in The Block (2019 article), not the original post, which I did not retrieve. Start date is the earliest affected-transaction date cited.

episodes.description: Severe fiat deposit/withdrawal delays by May 2018 (some customers never paid, some refunded after about six months) as Crypto Capital's accounts were closed/frozen; Crypto Capital voted to dissolve 2018-06-13.
episodes.notes: First report date is the earliest retrospective source I verified (The Block 2019-04-30); contemporaneous customer reports from May-June 2018 very likely exist but were not located, so the true first public report is probably earlier. Start 'by May 2018' is approximate; end date is a placeholder for 'through year-end', merging into BFX-2018-04.

episodes.description: Reports (Bloomberg, relayed by Cointelegraph) that Puerto Rico's Noble Bank, allegedly servicing Bitfinex/Tether, was in financial distress and seeking a buyer; Bitfinex later reported banking via HSBC.
episodes.notes: Noble Bank trouble first reported 2018-09-30 per Cointelegraph magazine (published 2018-10-20); I did not retrieve the Bloomberg original. Wikipedia (secondary) says the Noble relationship was terminated in September 2018; I found no source confirming Noble closed Bitfinex's account. Bitfinex said the reports did not affect operations.

episodes.description: Bitfinex paused fiat (USD, EUR, JPY, GBP) wire deposits; comms director Kasper Rasmussen confirmed on 2018-10-12 that deposits were temporarily paused for about a week; withdrawals continued. Bitfinex announced an 'improved' deposit system on 2018-10-16.
episodes.notes: First report is from customer screenshots circulated 2018-10-11 (Bitcoinist, dated by embedded tweet), confirmed 2018-10-12. End date is the 2018-10-16 announcement, not a verified restart time; Bitfinex's own Oct-15 release says deposits were paused 'for certain user groups'. Coindesk 2018-10-16 article could not be fetched (timeout) but its headline/summary was seen in search.

episodes.description: Bitfinex restarted USD fiat deposits for KYC-verified users via a 'new, improved' system, with deposits processed in roughly six to ten days.
episodes.notes: Restoration was partial (KYC-verified users, slow processing); Crypto Capital-routed flows were still failing in Nov-Dec 2018 (see BFX-2018-06).

episodes.description: Crypto Capital, Bitfinex's main retail fiat processor, could no longer process any fiat deposits/withdrawals by Dec 2018; about $851m of Bitfinex/Tether funds were reported lost, or seized per Bitfinex. Disclosed by the NYAG complaint (dated 2019-04-24, reported 2019-04-25).
episodes.notes: Rail failure itself was concealed ('small backlog' per chat logs) so the first PUBLIC report is the NYAG action. Start 2018-12 is from chat logs reported by The Block; NYAG links withdrawal struggles to Oct 2018. Loss vs seizure disputed. No documented end; Bitfinex sought discovery to recover funds in Oct 2019.

episodes.description: NYAG lawsuit and preliminary injunction (2019-04-25) against Bitfinex/Tether over concealed Crypto Capital loss; net outflows of about $585m in five days. Same cluster as BFX-2018-06; treat as a regulatory/confidence shock.
episodes.notes: Listed separately so a detector alarm on 2019-04-25 to 05-01 can be classified as the NYAG disclosure shock versus the underlying rail failure.

episodes.description: Bitfinex trading halted by an infrastructure-provider outage and a DDoS attack; trading resumed about 11am ET same day; no fund impact.
episodes.notes: Search summary of CNBC; page itself not fetched.

episodes.description: NYAG settlement with Bitfinex/Tether: $18.5m penalty, quarterly Tether reserve reports; no fiat-rail impact.
episodes.notes: Regulatory resolution of the 2019 case; no new impairment.

episodes.description: US DOJ arrests Lichtenstein and Morgan and seizes about 94,000 BTC tied to the 2016 Bitfinex hack; no fiat-rail impact.
episodes.notes: Date taken from the secondary reports (arrest announced 2022-02-08); no primary DOJ page retrieved.

episodes.description: Court filings show a dispute with former payment processor CNG Processing (US accounts at Citibank/BofA delayed and limited; about $2.7m of deposit and client funds allegedly frozen). Some outlets reported fiat withdrawal glitches; Bitstamp said it was processing fiat withdrawals.
episodes.notes: Fiat impact on customers is NOT confirmed (Bitstamp denied it; Bitstamp said it had not used CNG for over a year). Impairment window unknown. Low-confidence rail label; consider excluding from positives.

episodes.description: Bitstamp temporarily ended Silvergate Exchange Network service and USD wire support via Silvergate; said customer funds were safe, it had 17 banking partners and alternative rails in place (Signature Signet used for instant USD).
episodes.notes: Bitstamp's own blog post not retrieved. CryptoSlate dates it 2023-03-02; Odaily dates it 2023-03-03. No source found on what happened to Bitstamp's Signet USD rail after Signature closed on 2023-03-12 and no restoration date found.

episodes.description: Barclays ended its UK banking relationship with Coinbase (CoinDesk report); GBP Faster Payments access lost so UK fiat deposits/withdrawals took days; ClearBank expected to restore by end of Q3 2019.
episodes.notes: GBP rail, not USD: likely outside a USD-ledger test; keep as a venue-level fiat-rail event. Start date not documented; restoration only expected, not confirmed. Original CoinDesk article not retrieved.

episodes.description: Technical ACH problem blocked US bank-account payments/withdrawals on Coinbase for about six hours (6:57 to 12:41 ET); Coinbase said funds were safe.
episodes.notes: Times are from a search-result summary of the CoinDesk/Blockworks reports (those pages could not be fetched). Technical outage, not a banking-partner loss; best treated as a short rail glitch / near-confounder.

episodes.description: Coinbase stopped accepting or initiating payments to/from Silvergate and moved to other banks (including Signature); said client funds remained safe and accessible, with de minimis corporate exposure.
episodes.notes: No customer-facing USD impairment reported by Coinbase; label is partner loss, not a confirmed user-facing suspension.

episodes.description: Coinbase paused support for Signature Bank's Signet from 2023-03-20 until further notice (WSJ-reported, spokesperson-confirmed); USD deposits/withdrawals lost 24/7 instant rail and were limited to banking hours; USDC conversions stayed 24/7. Signature had been closed 2023-03-12.
episodes.notes: No restoration date found. Signet itself kept operating under FDIC receivership; the pause was Coinbase's choice. Coinbase had about $240m at Signature, expected to be fully recovered (FXStreet, secondary).

episodes.description: Coinbase paused USDC:USD conversions over the weekend while banks were closed after Circle disclosed $3.3bn SVB exposure; USDC fell as low as about $0.88 on 2023-03-11.
episodes.notes: Affects USDC redeemability, not Coinbase's USD ledger balances, but is the cleanest confounder for any USD/USDC basis signal in the SVB/Signature window. End 2023-03-13 is the planned Monday restart; actual restart not verified.

episodes.description: Coinbase disclosed an SEC Wells notice (8-K, 2023-03-22); services operated as usual; shares fell about 13% after hours.
episodes.notes: Regulatory action without fiat impact.

episodes.description: SEC sues Coinbase (unregistered exchange/broker/clearing agency); stock fell about 15% pre-market; USD services unaffected.
episodes.notes: Regulatory action without fiat impact, one day after the SEC suit against Binance/Binance.US.

episodes.description: Rumours that Bank of America closed personal accounts of Coinbase users; Armstrong polled followers (about 9% yes); no exchange-level USD rail impact.
episodes.notes: Individual-account debanking, not a Coinbase rail event; recorded only so alarms in July 2023 can be classified.

episodes.description: Planned two-hour maintenance turned into about a two-day outage after a trading-engine overhaul failed; all trading and withdrawals were suspended; funds intact.
episodes.notes: Start/end days taken from summaries (outage began 'last Thursday' = 2018-01-11, ended 2018-01-13); not checked against Kraken's own post.

episodes.description: Delays at Kraken's wire processor for domestic US USD deposits via Evolve Bank (status page 2020-06-29 23:24 UTC); deposits stuck 'Confirming' for extra business days; Kraken added an MVB USD funding option around 2020-07-07.
episodes.notes: First-report date is a user tweet (2020-06-25) cited by Finance Magnates; Kraken's status-page notice (primary) is 2020-06-29, FM article 2020-06-30. Deposit-side delay only. No resolution date; the MVB announcement is a workaround, not an end.

episodes.description: Per a Bloomberg report of a Kraken email, non-corporate clients would lose USD deposits/withdrawals through Signature Bank; on 2023-03-12 (Signature closed) Kraken said Signature/Signet deposits and withdrawals were processing as usual.
episodes.notes: Bloomberg original not retrieved (date 2023-03-01 inferred from Unchained's 'Wednesday report'). Start 2023-03-15 comes only from a search snippet of Blockworks (deposits ending 15 March), which returned 403; low confidence. Whether the restriction ever took effect after Signature's closure is unclear.

episodes.description: Kraken emailed customers on 2023-03-22 that ACH deposits (Plaid) and ACH withdrawals via Silvergate would end 2023-03-27 after Silvergate's SEN shutdown; Fedwire via MVB Bank and ACH instant purchases remained.
episodes.notes: First public report is the CoinDesk article of 2023-03-22/23 (CoinDesk fetch not attempted; Finance Magnates 2023-03-23 fetched). No restoration date found; Kraken's support page now lists ACH via Plaid but the return date is not documented.

episodes.description: SEC settlement: $30m and Kraken ends US staking-as-a-service; no fiat impact.
episodes.notes: Regulatory action without fiat impact.

episodes.description: WSJ (via ForkLog): Binance.US lost Signature and Silvergate as dollar banks, was routing fiat through intermediaries including Prime Trust, and failed to land Cross River and Customers Bancorp.
episodes.notes: WSJ original not retrieved; ForkLog date 2023-04-09 may lag WSJ by a day. Start set to the Signature closure date as the likely trigger; Binance.US's own timing of its exposure not documented. No USD service interruption was reported for Binance.US at this point.

episodes.description: Binance.US suspended USD deposits and warned banking partners would pause fiat withdrawals as early as 2023-06-13, citing the SEC lawsuit; users told to withdraw USD by 2023-06-13 and balances may be converted to stablecoins after 06-15.
episodes.notes: The Block published 2023-06-08 23:28 EDT = 2023-06-09 UTC. Start 2023-06-08 is local-time (Unchained and The Block say Thursday 8 June; ForkLog says June 9). End: see BUS-2025-01.

episodes.description: ACH USD withdrawals warned to take several days; delays built up and on 2023-06-22 Binance.US said it had cleared nearly all delayed USD withdrawals but expected banking partners to discontinue the service soon.
episodes.notes: The anticipated 2023-06-13 bank cutoff did not happen on schedule per CryptoSlate (one FXStreet piece says banks left on 06-13; sources conflict). End date is the 'mostly resolved' email, not a clean restoration.

episodes.description: Binance.US ran crypto-only with no USD fiat deposits or withdrawals (USD pairs removed, most delisted by 2023-07-13) until fiat was restored in February 2025.
episodes.notes: Exact date USD withdrawals ended is not established: The Block says fiat services were suspended in June 2023 and crypto-only from July 2023; the support article gives 2023-07-13 for removal of USD pairs. Start 2023-07-13 is therefore approximate (could be late June). End 2025-02-18 = day before restoration announcement.

episodes.description: Binance.US restored USD ACH deposits and withdrawals for the first time since June 2023 (rolled out gradually; initially about 10 assets tradable against USD).
episodes.notes: Announced 2025-02-19 08:45 EST (The Block); the rollout to all eligible users was gradual over following days.

episodes.description: SEC sues Binance, Binance.US and Changpeng Zhao (2023-06-05); on 2023-06-06 the SEC sought to freeze Binance.US assets, a compromise was approved by 2023-06-17. Direct cause of BUS-2023-02 to -04.
episodes.notes: Cause rather than independent confounder; use to separate 'SEC headline' from 'rail loss' in the first week of June. Suit date from ForkLog summary (2023-06-23); SEC primary document not retrieved. The 2025-02-13 court stay (60 days) is a minor related regulatory step.

context_events.event: Silvergate announces end of Silvergate Exchange Network (SEN) (2023-03-03) and wind-down/voluntary liquidation of the bank (2023-03-08)
NYDFS takes possession of Signature Bank; FDIC named receiver; Signet unit left outside the Flagstar sale announced 2023-03-19/20
Binance (global, not Binance.US) suspends USD bank transfers from 2023-02-08 after Signature capped payments; out of scope as a venue, noted as context
